I guess this started around seven months ago. At first it was more like I just…shut down inside. I used to be pretty proud of being a good nurse, picking up extra shifts, studying for specialty certs. Now when someone compliments my work, I just feel nothing. Finishing a hard shift, getting good feedback, even payday—it’s all kind of flat, like it’s happening to someone else. I move slower at work; my charge nurse has commented that I’m “dragging.” Even simple things—hanging IVs, walking down the hall—I feel like I’m moving through syrup.

Sleep is weird. I fall asleep okay, but I’m waking up at three or four almost every morning, wide awake, just lying there. I’m exhausted but can’t fall back asleep, and then I’m slow all day.

The other stuff started maybe a month after that? Six months, give or take. Sometimes I feel like the TV anchors are hinting about me, or that staff at the nurses’ station lower their voices because they’re talking specifically about what I did. I also sometimes see a man standing at the end of the hallway or in my room, but when I look straight at him, he’s gone. When I try to explain what’s going on, I catch myself jumping from one thing to another and losing track of what I was saying, even with patients or during report. I’m still working, but it’s getting harder to keep up.
D007-D015_h001.question_a:
I’ve been feeling “off” for about seven months now. At first it was mostly this heavy dullness, like someone turned the volume down on all my feelings. Things that used to matter—finishing a tough shift, getting praise from my charge nurse—barely register. I’m still going to work, but I move so slowly my coworkers comment on it, like I’m wading through water just to get from one patient room to the next. I wake up at 3 or 4 a.m. most days and just stare at the ceiling; I can’t fall back asleep and I don’t even care enough to try relaxation tricks anymore.

For the last six months I’ve also been convinced that small things are secretly about me—like when two nurses are talking quietly, I “know” they’re discussing how dangerous I am, or a random song playing in the hallway feels like it’s sending me a message. I sometimes see a man in dark scrubs standing at the end of the corridor or in my apartment, but when I look properly, he’s not there.

There was a stretch about a month ago, maybe two or three weeks, when that numb, slowed-down feeling actually lifted a bit—I could laugh with a coworker—but the sense that people were sending me signals and the shadowy man at the end of the hall were still there, just as strong.

My coworkers comment that I look “worn out.”

Sleep is awful. I wake up around 3 or 4 a.m. every day, completely awake, and just lie there, heavy, dreading the day. That’s usually when the other stuff happens. I’ll see a shadowy figure standing by my bedroom door, or someone sitting on the chair. When I turn on the light, no one’s there. On the bus or at work, I feel like the TV in the break room, the radio songs, even random conversations are aimed at me, hinting that I’ve done something wrong.

When I’m in this low state, my thoughts jump around when I talk, like I lose the thread mid-sentence. But these things only happen when I’m in this depressed phase—there hasn’t been a time I felt okay emotionally while still seeing things or feeling targeted. It’s really affecting my work; I’ve cut my hours and even basic tasks feel like wading through mud.

I used to enjoy my garden and the church knitting circle, but now I just sit in my chair and stare at the TV, not really watching. I don’t want to see friends, and even making a cup of tea feels like too much.

At night I lie there for hours, unable to fall asleep. My mind keeps going back to my husband, and I get this awful feeling that he was seeing someone else before he passed. I know that probably sounds silly at my age, and there’s nothing concrete, but I can’t shake the idea he was unfaithful. It makes me feel ashamed and angry.

Sometimes I see him standing in the doorway or sitting on the edge of the bed, clear as day, or I see shadowy figures moving in the hallway. When I try to explain this, my words get all tangled… it’s like they break apart in my mouth, and I lose track of what I’m trying to say. Even answering you now, I feel like I’m moving and talking through mud. It’s getting harder to manage the house and look after myself living alone.

I’ve been feeling really low for about seven months now. It’s like this heavy gray filter over everything. Stuff I used to enjoy—drawing for myself, going out with friends, even watching design videos—just feels flat. I mostly go to work, come home, and lie in bed. My speech has gotten… slow, I guess. People at the studio sometimes wait for me to answer and I can tell it’s awkward, but it’s like my words have to push through mud.

Sleep is bad. I keep having these intense, disturbing dreams—people getting hurt, or faces melting into strange shapes—and I wake up exhausted and scared. It happens most nights.

Around six months ago I also started seeing things that other people don’t seem to see. Sometimes when I’m walking to work, there are figures in the crowd that look too bright, like they’re outlined in neon, and then they vanish when I blink. At my desk I sometimes see symbols or patterns floating over the screen.

I’ve also gotten this strong sense that I’m… meant for something huge, like my designs are secretly influencing people worldwide, or that I can send messages through colors that change how others think. Part of me knows that sounds unrealistic, but it still feels true in the moment, and it all kind of mixes together with the low mood.

There was a couple of weeks where my mood actually felt more or less normal again, but the glowing figures and that certainty about my “destiny” didn’t go away. When I talk, especially on those days, my coworkers say I jump between ideas so much they can’t follow what I’m saying at all.
